properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/07/2020 to SWN PROD CO LLC in Independence Twp, Washington county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SWN PROD CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/05/2020
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 896393
Permit API: 125-27157
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Independence Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/07/2020
Comments: On October 5, 2020, I conducted a follow up inspection of the Fred Jones Well Site in Independence Township, Washington County. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported to the Department on 10/4/2020 (CID#352896) . The 10/4/2020 report indicated that approximately 630 gallons of brine was spilled to the well pad. I spoke with Operator representative Casey Barkus on 10/5/2020. Mr. Barkus indicated that a non-structural weld developed a pin hole in the brine tank and caused a stream of brine to shoot across the well pad. Mr. Barkus indicated that the release continued until the brine could be removed from the brine tank. Mr. Barkus indicated that the brine was contained on the well pad and that the pad drain valves were closed. Mr. Barkus indicated that the operator would be utilizing Act 2 clean up as a remediation standard.At the time of inspection, I spoke with operator Josh Boyda. The operator was utilizing third party contractors Miller Environmental and Moody and Associates to guide the remediation of the impacted area. The operator was utilizing a skid steer and excavator to removed impacted material. Mr. Boyda indicated that the impacted material has been placed in the roll off boxes and the crew is awaiting additional disposal boxes to be delivered. I observed 5 rolloff boxes staged within secondary containment and 2 more rolloff boxes located near the impacted area. Mr. Boyda indicated that approximately 12 yards of impacted material has been placed in each rolloff box. The impacted area appeared to be 100' x 60' area located between the brine tank battery and the fenced in well head area. Approximately 6” of material had been removed from the impacted area. Mr. Boyda showed me the non-structural weld on the brine tank that caused the release. The weld in question is located on the brine tank approximately 6' from the bottom of tank on the left side of the brine tank manufacturer information plate.I utilized a Spectrum Field Scout Direct Soil EC meter to screen for conductivity. I screened the impacted area, outlet location and the standing water within the pad drain system.At the impacted area near the fenced well head the meter indicated conductivity of 8.75 mS/cm.At the approximately center of the impacted area of the well pad the meter indicated conductivity of 12.80 mS/cm.At the storm water inlet in the northwest corner of the well pad the meter indicated that conductivity was Or (Or is over range. The meter's max conductivity limit is 20 mS/cm).At the outlet of the pad drain on the meter indicated that conductivity was 0.5 mS/cm.The pad drain outlet appeared to be closed. I recommend that the Operator removed the standing fluid from the outlet and keep the pad drain valve close until remediation is finished and verified.The operator is in compliance with the Department spill policy for reporting and remediation of spills greater than 42 gallons.Violations are being issued for the failure to control a regulated fluid resulting in a release to the ground.The Department requests clarification of how the Operator calculated the amount of fluid released.

SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/29/2022
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 959039
Permit API: 081-21885
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/09/2022
Comments: An incident inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that a release of an estimated 5 barrels of produced water occurred which then overflowed secondary containment during completion operations on Pad B. I met with Rick Hall of EQT upon arriving on location. According to Mr. Hall, a hose failed which was hooked up to a booster pump that was being used for coiled tubing operations at the time of the release. After the secondary containment overflowed, the produced water flowed toward the stormwater channel along the pad edge. Mr. Hall said that he would have a sump dug in the stormwater channel at the pad edge to attempt to recover as much of the release as possible. Due to the amount of equipment on the pad and the waterlines and electrical cables along the side of the pad, Hall said that little excavation would be possible until completion operations were finished. He said that completions may be done as soon as the middle of July. He also said that Creston Environmental was en route to conduct screening of the site. Due to the volume of fluid which was released from the failed hose and the unknown volume of fluid released to the pad surface, the Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation. Violations remain outstanding for the March 29, 2022 release on Pad B.

Comments: On 12/27/2024 an Incident Response inspection was conducted the MOR42 Well Site in response to an operator reported release.On 12/27/2024 CNX Resources Representative, Ben Geary, reported an approximately 40-gallon brine release off containment at the MOR42 Well Pad located in East Finley Township, Washington County.CNX Resources representative, Ben Geary, and SPSI representative, Mac Maydak, were on site at time of inspection. Mr. Geary informed the Department that that the release was discovered on Saturday, January 25 at 1:15 pm, that the quantity released was approximately 40 gallons, and that a contractor (SPSI) had been dispatched the same day. Mr. Maydak stated that his crew was dispatched on Saturday (1/25) at approximately 1:40 pm. The origin of the release was stated to be a crack found on a T-joint along a line connecting to a slug catcher to the production tanks, which could be observed in front of the Unit H Gas Processing Unit (GPU).Mr. Geary stated that remediation efforts had taken place Saturday (1/25), Sunday (1/26), and continued into today (1/27). The area remediated at the time of inspection measured approximately 38 by 18 feet and to a depth of 1 inch, excluding the sump created on the western side of the GPU that measured approximately 8 inches in depth. It was made known that field screening was conducted during the remediation efforts with screening values between 2,000 and 12,000 s/cm observed. Mr. Maydak stated that 4 Vac boxes had been filled with removed material at the time of inspection.Mr. Geary stated that the remediation efforts would continue until all conductivity values were below 3,000 s/cm and that the sump would be monitored and any fluid that appears would be screened and removed via vac truck.PA DEP Conductivity probe calibrated on 12/27/2024.The following was observed during the inspection:-The Act 9 sign was present at the site entrance (Photo 1).-A crew was on site remediating near the Unit H GPU. A vac truck and vac box were observed near the remediation site (Photos 2-3).-The remediation area near the Unit H GPU and the source of the release were observed. A crack was observed on the T-joint of a line beneath a lock out-tag out tag. The lines appeared to be coated in a white film, obscuring visual observations (Photos 4-6).-The excavated areas located in front of and on the west side of the GPU were observed. It appeared that pad aggregate had been removed down to the larger riprap (Photos 7-8).-Field soil conductivity screening was conducted in various locations of the remediation site. The bottom and side walls of the sump were screened, with conductivity values ranging between1.682 ms/cm(1,682s/cm) and 4.71 ms/cm observed. Screening was conducted along the northern edge of the GPU and values of 2.56 ms/cm and 1.927 ms/cm (1,682s/cm) were observed. An area in front of the adjacent equipment on the western side of the GPU was screened. Values in this area ranged between 2.66 ms/cm and 11.69 ms/cm (Photos 9 -16).Determination:Violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued for the release. A violation of 78a64a(a) is being issued for the lack of secondary containment.

properties.summary: Administrative violation issued on 2016-12-02 to Apex Energy (Pa) Llc in Penn Twp, Westmoreland county. 78a55(b) - CONTROL AND DISPOSAL PLANNING  – PPC Plan - Operator failed to prepare and develop a site specific PPC plan prior to storing, using, or generating regulated substances on a well site from the drilling, alteration, production, plugging or other activity associated with a gas well or transporting those regulated substances to, on or from a well site.

Report Details

Violation ID 774277
Permit API 129-28892
Unconventional Y

Municipality Penn Twp

Inspection Date 2016-12-02
Comments Inspection performed in response to Emergency Response Team’s (ERT) request for a Department follow-up to an odor complaint received by ERT on 12/1/2016. NRC Incident Report (#1165394) relating to odor complaint stated a release of 2 ounces of mercaptan (odorant) from the unconventional drill pad due to unknown reasons. Prior to this inspection, Emergency Response Incident Report and Operator stated initial clean-up measures on the day of the incident consisted of the removal of three sealed 5 gallon plastic buckets of impacted soil. Operator stated that Deomer (deodorant) to neutralize the smell of the mercaptan was applied on the impacted area. A plastic mat/tarp was also placed over the impacted area to suppress the odor until remediation of the soil could be conducted the next day. On 12/2/2016 @ 11:00 WQS-Alawattegama, OGI-Braunns and AQS-Miller arrived on site to conduct a joint inspection. At the time of inspection, Lance Casaday, Jim Drinkwine (contractors for Operator) and, clean-up crew were present on site. Operator explained that Apex Energy personnel were in the process of performing scheduled maintenance work that involved replacing the manifold that is attached to a 1000 gallon mercaptan tank. At around 11:30am operator personnel damaged the 1/4” line connected to the mercaptan tank. This line had approximately 2-3 ounces of residual mercaptan that was released to the ground. Operator estimates that the 1000 gallon tank had less than 30 gallons of mercaptan at the time of the incident. Spill occurred on the gravel well pad beneath the mercaptan line. Impacted area measured approximately 15’x15’. Clean-up operations had not yet commenced at the time of inspection. The Department did not detect any odors until within 6-10ft of the impacted area. An Altair 5x gas meter was used to conduct gas monitoring (VOC’s H2S, CO, and combustibles) of the air in the vicinity of the (unexcavated) impacted area. The meters did not indicate the presence of VOC’s, H2S, CO, or combustible gas at the time of inspection. During the inspection, clean-up crew proceeded with excavating the impacted soil and gravel which was placed in steel drums and sealed pending appropriate disposal. Altair 5x gas meter was used to conduct gas monitoring (VOC’s H2S, CO, and combustibles) of the air in the vicinity of the excavated (impacted) area. The meters did not indicate the presence of VOC’s, H2S, CO, or combustible gas at the time of inspection. The 1,000 gallon mercaptan tank was located within secondary containment and both the tank and containment appeared structurally sound. The odorant mercaptan tank was not labeled at the time of inspection. PPC and ER plans were located on site. PPC plan does not appear to be site specific as mercaptan was not listed as a material being stored at this specific well site. ER plan did not include Safety Data (SD) sheets for the odorant (Mercaptan) and deodorant (Deomer). Department requested Operator provide a written report detailing the cause, nature of release, and actions taken to remediate and future actions/plans to prevent such incidents as well as copies of SD sheets for chemicals released and applied as a result of the odorant release. Department also requests Operator explain how volume of odorant released was estimated (e.g. odorant tank readings before and after release) and/or any other means. Violations are being issued under 25 PA CODE 78a. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending Departmental investigation. Department will conduct a follow-up inspection. Department will conduct follow-up inspection. Permit API: 015-23540
Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/17/2022
Comments: On 8/17/2022, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an incident inspection in response to a spill at the Chesapeake MTL well site. The spill Complaint ID 366296 was received by the department on 8/17/2022. It was 75 degrees and overcast when I arrived on location. The spill was reported as an estimated 40 gallons of produced water released to the ground due to a dump line failure on the produced water tank. The initial impacted area was reported as 5'x5'. When I arrived on location, i viewed the area around the production tank. A flow back tank was nearby, a vacuum truck was being set up near the production tank and a man lift was next to the tank. I witnessed orange paint on the ground enclosing an estimated 6'x8' foot area on the north side of the tank with dark-stained ground and enclosing an estimated 20'x20' area on the south side of the tank with lighter stained ground.I met Chesapeake's production manager Gordon Fleming. He said that he did not know the specifics of the spill but that the four wells were shut in and a crew was on site to vacuum the liquids and solids out of the production tank. The tank was going to be moved to a temporary location so the spill area, including the area under the tank, could be excavated. Gordon said that the flowback tank was going to be used for production fluids while the equipment and area associated with the spill were excavated, cleaned, repaired, and put back into service. While the vac truck crew was setting up, I viewed the contaminated area. I field tested the soil in the area marked off on the north side of the tank for conductivity with results of 1,720 uS next to the north side of the tank, 718 uS 6 feet to the northwest and 4 uS 5 feet to the northeast. Gordon put me in contact with Chesapeake's Environmental Representative Danielle Schaad who reported the following: The spill was witnessed by the lease operator who was in the process of stimulating the wells and was unloading fluids from the wells to the production tank. The piping above the tank washed out, causing the release. After reporting the spill, Chesapeake brought a drone to location to observe the area around the production tank from the air in order to visibly determine the extent of the spill. The orange paint on the ground marked the visual extent of the contamination. After the vac crew cleans the tank, it will be moved to the side, away from the contaminated area. Creston Environmental is being mobilized to the site and expected to start testing and excavating the contaminated area on 8/18/2022 at 8:00 hrs. Danielle said that Chesapeake was holding with the 40-gallon estimation of the spill until Creston Environmental is able to determine the extent of contamination and give a better estimation. The release of production fluid to the unprotected pad surface constitutes a violation of Section 402 of the Clean Streams Law, of 78A57(a) for improper control, storage and disposal of production fluids and SWMA 301 for improper management of residual waste. The department also recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation in accordance with 78a.66 due to the extent of the contamination and the estimation being close to the 42-gallon action level.I left the site at 16:10 hrs.On 8/18/2022 at 14:30 I arrived back at location to view the progress with the excavation. During the visit, I took pictures 14-21.I met with Danielle Schaad and with Creston Environmental Andrew Steffe. The excavated area was 35'x16'x2' and field tested at 995 uS conductance or less. Samples for laboratory testing were collected. Danielle did report that Chesapeake would pursue Act 2 Remediation. I did witness the excavated material piled up on plastic secondary containment. I did request a copy of the manifest upon disposal. As I was leaving the site, the excavated area was being filled in with clean material.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/25/2026
Violation Code: 78a66(b)2 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases - Operator or other responsible party failed to contact the appropriate regional Department office by telephone or call the Department’s Statewide toll free number as soon as practicable, but no later than 2 hours after discovering the spill or release.
Violation ID: 8268726
Permit API: 015-23994
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Pike Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/25/2026
Comments: On 03/24/2026 at 1132 hours Repsol reported (CTS#396090) that at 0600 hours they noticed fluid in the southside ditch of the Ugliuzza well pad that was going towards the catch basin. There was a hose that did not have a cap on it and the fluid was coming from the hose. They are estimating ~630 gallons (1 barrel=42 gallons) of produced water was released off containment. Resource Management was contracted to conduct remediation. At ~1525 hours Repsol contacted the DEP to update the amount release to be ~18,900 gallons. Four water trucks off-loading onsite each contained 4,620 gallons of produced fluid. It is estimated that the release traveled 1,143 feet downhill to the stream. A remediation plan is in place, and they are implementing it as we spoke. On 03/23/2026 at 2218 hours the first of five water trucks arrived onsite to off-load fluid for upcoming completion activities. From 2218-0319 hours 4 water trucks off-loaded onsite. At 0615 hours on 03/24/2026 a 5th water truck started offloading and immediately noticed the leak and stopped off-loading. On 03/25/2026 Repsol reported that as of 0700 hours ~10,500 gallons of fluid had been recovered from the stormwater channel and basin. On 03/25/2026 the DEP conducted an incident inspection report of Repsol's UGLIUZZA Well Pad. Water Quality Specialists Korey Starkey, Jonathan Pennings and I arrived at ~ 0930 hours. Licensed Professional Geologist Samuel Louderback arrived at approximately 1100 hours. The DEP met with Repsol representative Meagan DePue and Resource Management. Fenton Excavation was onsite excavating within the LOD to capture fluids during the inspection. Meagan stated that she contacted the PFBC and left a message. She informed us that a hose connected to the manifold was not connected to the produced fluid tanks and that it was hanging over the side of the secondary containment into the stormwater ditch while the first four trucks off-loaded (photo #2-6). The produced fluid then flowed to the stormwater basin (photo #7) and through the drainage pipe of the stormwater basin (photo #9) into a natural conveyance channel which reached a UNT to Rockwell Creek. The DEP, Repsol and Resource Management walked the impacted area together. Resource Management set up monitoring points and split sampled during that time. The fluids in the stormwater ditch were field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) at ~7.85 mS/cm. There was a sump pump in the stormwater ditch (photo #5). A sample was collected from the stormwater basin at 1204 hours (photo #8). The EC of the sampled fluids were >19.99 mS/cm. Fluids were able to escape the basin through an outflow pipe. Two sumps were constructed inside and outside of the basin (photo #7 and 10). Fluids collected in the sumps were being actively recovered.The EC of the drainage area beyond the stormwater basin was ~1.8 mS/cm and the soil EC was ~4.8 mS/cm (photo #11). The drainage area forms a conveyance channel ~500ft down from the release location. The EC of the conveyance channel was ~5.4 mS/cm (photo #12). There was a spring adding water to the channel ~900ft downstream from the release location. It was located above grade (photo #13). The EC of the spring was ~100 us/cm. We traveled ~500ft downstream the conveyance channel and obtained EC readings between 2.6-2.7 mS/cm (photo #14 and 15).We traveled downstream ~435ft. The conveyance channel EC was between 5.8-8.0 mS/cm (photo #16 and 17). The DEP and Resource Management each collected a sample at 1053 hours from the UNT upstream of where the released fluids discharged into the stream (photo #18). The DEP and Resource Management each collected a sample at 1118 hours from the UNT downstream of where the released fluids discharged into the stream (photo #22).The EC of Rockwell Creek ~1.4 miles away was ~0.15 mS/cm.

Violation Code: 78a66(b)2 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases - Operator or other responsible party failed to contact the appropriate regional Department office by telephone or call the Department’s Statewide toll free number as soon as practicable, but no later than 2 hours after discovering the spill or release.
Violation ID: 8268726
Permit API: 015-23994
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Pike Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/25/2026
Comments: On 03/24/2026 at 1132 hours Repsol reported (CTS#396090) that at 0600 hours they noticed fluid in the southside ditch of the Ugliuzza well pad that was going towards the catch basin. There was a hose that did not have a cap on it and the fluid was coming from the hose. They are estimating ~630 gallons (1 barrel=42 gallons) of produced water was released off containment. Resource Management was contracted to conduct remediation. At ~1525 hours Repsol contacted the DEP to update the amount release to be ~18,900 gallons. Four water trucks off-loading onsite each contained 4,620 gallons of produced fluid. It is estimated that the release traveled 1,143 feet downhill to the stream. A remediation plan is in place, and they are implementing it as we spoke. On 03/23/2026 at 2218 hours the first of five water trucks arrived onsite to off-load fluid for upcoming completion activities. From 2218-0319 hours 4 water trucks off-loaded onsite. At 0615 hours on 03/24/2026 a 5th water truck started offloading and immediately noticed the leak and stopped off-loading. On 03/25/2026 Repsol reported that as of 0700 hours ~10,500 gallons of fluid had been recovered from the stormwater channel and basin. On 03/25/2026 the DEP conducted an incident inspection report of Repsol's UGLIUZZA Well Pad. Water Quality Specialists Korey Starkey, Jonathan Pennings and I arrived at ~ 0930 hours. Licensed Professional Geologist Samuel Louderback arrived at approximately 1100 hours. The DEP met with Repsol representative Meagan DePue and Resource Management. Fenton Excavation was onsite excavating within the LOD to capture fluids during the inspection. Meagan stated that she contacted the PFBC and left a message. She informed us that a hose connected to the manifold was not connected to the produced fluid tanks and that it was hanging over the side of the secondary containment into the stormwater ditch while the first four trucks off-loaded (photo #2-6). The produced fluid then flowed to the stormwater basin (photo #7) and through the drainage pipe of the stormwater basin (photo #9) into a natural conveyance channel which reached a UNT to Rockwell Creek. The DEP, Repsol and Resource Management walked the impacted area together. Resource Management set up monitoring points and split sampled during that time. The fluids in the stormwater ditch were field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) at ~7.85 mS/cm. There was a sump pump in the stormwater ditch (photo #5). A sample was collected from the stormwater basin at 1204 hours (photo #8). The EC of the sampled fluids were >19.99 mS/cm. Fluids were able to escape the basin through an outflow pipe. Two sumps were constructed inside and outside of the basin (photo #7 and 10). Fluids collected in the sumps were being actively recovered.The EC of the drainage area beyond the stormwater basin was ~1.8 mS/cm and the soil EC was ~4.8 mS/cm (photo #11). The drainage area forms a conveyance channel ~500ft down from the release location. The EC of the conveyance channel was ~5.4 mS/cm (photo #12). There was a spring adding water to the channel ~900ft downstream from the release location. It was located above grade (photo #13). The EC of the spring was ~100 us/cm. We traveled ~500ft downstream the conveyance channel and obtained EC readings between 2.6-2.7 mS/cm (photo #14 and 15).We traveled downstream ~435ft. The conveyance channel EC was between 5.8-8.0 mS/cm (photo #16 and 17). The DEP and Resource Management each collected a sample at 1053 hours from the UNT upstream of where the released fluids discharged into the stream (photo #18). The DEP and Resource Management each collected a sample at 1118 hours from the UNT downstream of where the released fluids discharged into the stream (photo #22).The EC of Rockwell Creek ~1.4 miles away was ~0.15 mS/cm.

Comments: This inspection is taking place in response to a spill reported by the operator on 8/30/2020 at approximately 3:30 PM. According to the operator, due to human error a shut valve was left open which allowed reuse water to travel from the tank pad to the well pad storage tanks which then over flowed into secondary containment. An additional amount appeared to splash off into the R3 riprap adjacent to the secondary containment. SPSI was dispatched to remediate the off containment spill and a vacuum truck was already on site to remove what was lost to secondary containment.According to the operator 1,043 gallons was removed from secondary containment. 5-7 gallons is reported to have been lost off containment.On my arrival I was met by operator representative Brandon Carson and Jason Dockum Water Supervisor. The site is actively being frac'd, but is down for an inspection. SPSI is not on site, the operator reports that remediation efforts have been completed and a single roll off box is awaiting pick up (Photo 10).The ERP is on site in the mailbox. Safety Data Sheets are located in the trailer along with the secondary containment log (Photo 9). The secondary containment was inspected on both 8/30 and 8/31. No leaks to containment were reported and no visible leaks are currently observed.There is still a rust colored fluid in secondary containment (Photo 2). According to the operator, the mats are being washed off and a vac truck is on site to remove the water. The operator reports that this is not from the spill incident.The operator reports that the over flow was observed immediately and the shut in valve to the storm drain was closed (Photo 4). No sheen is observed in the drain or at the PCSM feature (Photo 6, 7, & 8).The operator reports that the valve will be closed until the next rain to verify everything was adequately cleaned.Visually impacted material appears to have been remediated (Photo 1, 3, & 5). The visually remediated area was probed for conductivity, nothing over .5 Sm was detected.The Department requests that the waste manifest be submitted to the Department as soon as possible.Based on this inspection violations are being noted as immediately corrected. Pending receipt of the waste manifest, and further investigation, more violations may be issued.

Permit API: 031-23576
Unconventional: No
County: Clarion
Municipality: Clarion Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/04/2021
Comments: This is a well located within 2500' of an active gas migration area. At the time of inspection, well was equipped to produce. The tubing valve was closed, but the 4 1/2" was tied in and the valve pinched open. The annulus was closed. The well integrity appeared good at surface and no leaks were detected. However, I picked up as high as 46% LEL in the ground outside of the wellhead, farthest from the tank and then 8% gas between the wellhead and tank. Due to this, there is a problem with the well integrity downhole and the well is in violation. The well was labeled and equipped with a check calve, separator, line heater, regulator, and chart (last changed on 9/13). There was also a 100 bbl fiberglass tank tied in. The compressor had been shut off on September 28th, as you can see on the Barton chart where there is a pressure increase.

Comments: On May 7, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Chabal 2 well site in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3967072 where violations issued from IR 3965337 were left outstanding. During the time of IR 3967072, it appeared that excavation and remediation work had started onsite as a covered excavation stockpile was observed at the well site.The following was observed:The well head is equipped with a well tag appears to be free of fluid leaks at the time of inspection (see photo 3). The operator's information is posted on the separator (see photo 4). The body of the brine tank appears to be sound at the time of inspection (see photos 5). The covered excavation stockpile that was observed onsite during the time IR 3967072 remains, in addition to another covered excavation stockpile at the downslope end of the impacted area. They appear to be from remediation work that has been conducted thus far (see photos 6, 9, and 11). The path of brown staining that was observed traveling downslope from the brine tank during the time of IR 3965337 remains covered with plastic sheeting, and appears to have been excavated near the brine tank and the downslope end of the impacted area (see photos 7, 8, and 10). Oil absorbent booms remain placed downslope of the covered impacted area (see photo 12). No evidence of visual impacts and/or elevated conductivity were detected downslope of impacted area (see photos 14 and 15).Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that remediation work remains ongoing and the impacted area remains adequately protected to mitigate risk of the impact being spread by stormwater.Violations issued from IR 3965337 shall remain outstanding.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Permit API: 105-21962
Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter
Municipality: Hector Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/01/2025
Comments: On 05/01/2025 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Greylock Production LLCs Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 0930 hours, weather was 62F and sunny. An Act 9 sign is visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).Standing water observed on the pad surface field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) at a range of ~246-645us/cm.There are 2 wells tagged with American Petroleum Institute (API) numbers located onsite (photos #2 and 3). Personnel were onsite drilling top holes and setting conductors for 3 additional wells; they informed me that rig move in for well drilling would begin on approximately 05/15/2025. (photo #4). 2 gas processing units (GPUs) are also located onsite (photo #5). The GPUs are held in a secondary containment structure which held less than 10% standing water. There are 4 produced fluid tanks located onsite and stationed in secondary containment (photo #6); the containment structure contained less than 10% standing water. A dehydration unit is also noted and held in secondary containment (photo #7).Numerous temporary storage tanks are located onsite and contain produced fluids from flow back (photos #8 and 9). The temporary storage tanks are held in secondary containment. The upright brine storage tanks remain onsite and have been confirmed to be empty by personnel at Greylock (photo #10). Roll-off waste containers were also observed onsite and contain top hole drilling cuttings (photo #11).Areas surrounding the site are not yet permanently stabilized with greater than 70% uniform perennial vegetative cover. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. An erosion and sediment (E and S) inspection log is available for review and up to date (photo #12). 1 infiltration basin serves as the site's post construction stormwater management (PCSM) control (photo #13). No standing water was observed in the PCSM controls and they appear to be functioning as intended.Violations noted in inspection report #'s 3881391 and 3878285 remain outstanding against API #105-21962 pending receipt of confirmation sampling and approval of Act 2 remediation standards.No violations noted. I departed the site at 1030 hours.
